T-002.Title: Status and archive gate consume shared membership; token orphan triple

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: DependsOn T-001 is binding: consumers land only after the extracted definition exists. grace-status.ts imports membership from artifact/run-membership (not grace-cursor). Delete countOpenEpochs' readdirSync endsWith(".xml") predicate; open epoch = listLooseEvents(bundle).length > 0. Assert source-level absence of that readdir/endsWith open-epoch filter and of any grace-cursor import in grace-status.ts. When listRunOrphans length > 0, status surfaces orphans=N (explicit; see design D5). Assert via formatStatusText / collectProjectStatus.

evaluateArchiveGate: no-open-epoch remains listLooseEvents.length === 0 (predicate unchanged). When permitting and orphans exist, requirement message is **not** the string "run/ empty"; it states no foldable loose events and names orphan(s) (name and/or class) via listRunOrphans from the shared module. When run/ is truly empty, a truthful empty phrasing is allowed. Red-first: gate archive **--record=false** on a **mandatory temp copy** of the C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY run/ shape (never the live archived bundle — F18) currently messages "run/ empty" while NaN orphan exists — capture that false sentence in a failing regression before the wording fix. Live C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY is for read-only status and shasum only.

AC-TOKEN-ORPHAN-TRIPLE: (1) live NaN file SHA-1 still c0cc8899c264381766a18918e2109b5e05693893 (tests use copies; never mutate the live path); (2) evaluateArchiveGate / gate archive **--record=false** on a **temp copy** of the orphan-only run/ shape permits with message not "run/ empty" and names the orphan; (3) ngrace status on the live repository reports open=0 or omits open for C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY and shows an explicit orphan signal. One subject exercises F14 + F15 + counterweights.

AC-ARCHIVE-STILL-REFUSES-LOOSE (counterweight, same task): fixture with ≥1 foldable loose run/ event → evaluateArchiveGate **refuses** no-open-epoch. Honest wording must not permit open foldable epochs. Fixture only — never open a real loose epoch on a live archived bundle.

AC-STATUS-OPEN-FOLDS-WITH-GATE: orphan-only run/ → status open=0 + orphan signal; real foldable loose event → status open≥1. Agreement with the gate on foldable open-ness is via the shared import (T-001 construction), not a second predicate.

AC-MEMBERSHIP-ONE-DEFINITION complete: status and evaluateArchiveGate both consume the artifact/run-membership definition; T-001 === re-export proof still holds after consumer wiring; grace-status does not import grace-cursor and no longer owns an independent endsWith(".xml") open-epoch predicate.

For MustExist of active/<same-id>/… that exists under archive/<same-id>/, no review.confidently-wrong. T-004.Title: Scope audit lifecycle exclusion (F11) with ledger-invalid counterweight

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: auditScopeOutsideWriteScope (or review with --changed-files) on lifecycle-only porcelain under .ngrace/changes/{active,archive}/C-*/(run/** |run.xml|run-ledger.xml) with empty OWS for those paths currently raises review.scope-outside-write-scope — capture in a failing regression. Independent of membership/F16/P0 tasks.

AC-SCOPE-LIFECYCLE-EXCLUSION: those lifecycle paths for **any** change id produce zero scope-outside findings, including when the reviewed --change id differs from the bundle that owns the porcelain (fold of A must not error a review of B). An additional out-of-scope production/docs path (e.g. src/secret.ts) **still** raises scope-outside. Excluding all of .ngrace/changes/**, or requiring run/ in ObservedWriteScope to pass, fails this criterion. Do not exclude plan.xml / spec.xml.

AC-LEDGER-INVALID-STILL-CATCHES (counterweight, same task): a deliberately malformed run-ledger.xml Allocation or Event that today raises ledger.invalid-allocation or ledger.invalid-event (grammar / lint) still raises that code after the change. Scope silence on lifecycle paths is not silence on ledger content integrity. Assert via existing grammar/lint surface (no new detector required if grammar already covers the case).

Red-first: evaluateApplyGate / gate apply **--record=false** on an approved plan fixture (temp project — never a live archived bundle) with no usable Verdicts entry currently yields gate.apply.no-verdict with catalog title only or only "no Verdicts section entry" — capture that thin message. No flush/race work (0 hits / 50 cycles in derivation). Independent of other repairs. Use --record=false or --no-record only (F18: space form silently records).

AC-APPLY-VERDICT-DIAGNOSTICS: refuse path detail names (1) ledger path looked at or that run-ledger.xml is missing, (2) Verdict child count (0 for absence), (3) why the newest did not qualify (absent vs invalid with reason). Catalog title alone fails. After recordReviewVerdict and immediate evaluateApplyGate, decision is permit when other requirements hold — no flush required.

T-006.Title: Baseline lint framing line (P0.9) without severity downgrade

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: active approved plan with failing BaselineAssertions MustNotExist (fixture); formatTextReport has no baseline-expectations lead line today — capture that absence. Independent of other repairs.

AC-BASELINE-LINT-FRAMING: default text output **leads** with a line stating N baseline expectation(s) expected while C-* is in progress (wording may normalize whitespace). N is counted by construction at the BaselineAssertions evaluateSection call site and stored in a module-private WeakMap<LintResult, number> in lint/core.ts (design D3 / D13) — not by assertion.* code-prefix over all issues, not by a curated subset, not by a cast field on the result object. Underlying assertion.* issues remain **errors** (not deleted, not downgraded). Removing or skipping baseline evaluation fails. Archived plans' baselines stay syntax-only.

Counterweight / discriminating negatives in the same task: (1) issues stay errors; (2) TargetAssertions extraction issue does not inflate N; (3) no edit to src/lint/types.ts (M-LINT-TYPES not in AffectedAreas); (4) a test asserts the --format json output shape gains **no new key** (WeakMap must not leak onto the schemaVersion-bearing surface — fails under cast approach, passes under WeakMap; D13).
